indicators.note: the wife's letter goes into the opening, the gap, of the other word

parts.note: to present a dish is to serve it
W is the standard abbreviation for wife in genealogies and marriage records

explanation.surface: Someone dodges having their wife open a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve something is to veer aside from it, so to dodge or evade it.

parts.note: S is the head, the first letter, of the word soft

explanation.surface: A child's alphabet primer: S is for simpleton.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the answer: SOFT HEAD means the head of SOFT, which is S, so the clue's S is what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A softhead is a dim, foolish person, a dated term for a fool.

clue.text: Get rid of badly brewed ale in time

indicators.note: something badly brewed is concocted wrongly, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A brewer must dump a batch of beer that was poorly made in time.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove or dispose of something entirely.

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which is VI in Roman numerals
a champion is the king of their sport

explanation.surface: A boast that a sexual champion is a Nordic man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is not about intimacy: it is the Latin word for six, VI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings were seafaring Norse raiders from medieval Scandinavia, so a Viking is one such Norseman.

clue.text: Coppers joining plot put to death

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers or coppers
a plot of land is a patch

explanation.surface: Police officers join a conspiracy to carry out an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests coins or the chemical Cu, but here it means police: DI is detective inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them quickly, an idiom for executing.

indicators.note: something that erupts bursts apart, so these letters are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Family strain flares up the moment an aunt loses her temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something instantaneous happens at once, with no delay, which is what immediate means.

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head

indicators.note: in a down clue backing means the word is read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: A question whether a kneecapping, or a header, has universal support.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the anatomical name for the kneecap bone.

clue.text: Loudly muck about in US city

indicators.note: loudly means the word is said out loud and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: to muck about with something is to tamper with it

explanation.surface: Someone noisily fools around in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final R is silent, so TAMPER sounds like the Florida city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a large city on the west coast of Florida.

parts.note: being present, in attendance, is being here

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: its outer letters are S and Y

explanation.surface: Disagreement right now is very frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief at odds with accepted doctrine, so a form of dissent.

parts.note: Risk is a board game of world conquest

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the game' is British slang for working as a prostitute; here it is the board game Risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk someone is to search them by patting down their clothing.

clue.text: Drunkenly toast Emir in island state

indicators.note: something done drunkenly is unsteady and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy toast to a Gulf ruler during a visit to an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: East Timor (Timor-Leste) is a country occupying the eastern half of the island of Timor.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the act of founding or creating something
second meaning: a business premises, of which a shop is an example

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like opening a shop; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the founding of something and a business or institution such as a store.

parts.note: a shock is also a thick mass of hair, which a fine mesh holds in place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' suggests fright or electricity; a shock of hair is a bushy mop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine mesh worn to keep a mass of hair in place.

clue.text: Listening closely, as our new monarch is?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a jibe at King Charles III, often teased for his prominent ears

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is on King Charles III, who became monarch in 2022 and is famously caricatured with large ears.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone paying complete attention, as if made entirely of hearing organs.

clue.text: A yes from posh boy's nanny

parts.note: yah is an affected upper-class British way of saying yes

explanation.surface: A rich boy says yes to his nursemaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayah is a nursemaid or maid, a term from colonial India.

parts.note: late here means deceased, so this is a published notice of a death

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a warning about being behind time; 'the late' means the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's death notice reports someone has died and summarises their life.

parts.note: the Metropolitan Police, London's force, is known as Scotland Yard, so the Met's is Yard's
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A question about how good the London police's reputation is.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying on tick means buying on credit in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used for comparison, a figurative measure.

clue.text: M for title of Emmanuel Macron

definitions.meaning: first meaning: M is the abbreviation for the French honorific
second meaning: the French equivalent of Mr, his title as a Frenchman

explanation.walkthrough: Styled like an alphabet primer; M. is the written short form of the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsieur is the French courtesy title for a man, equivalent to Mr or sir.

indicators.note: a different arrangement of the letters is called for

clue.text: Magic party for the doctor, they say

explanation.walkthrough: A do held for Doctor Who would be a Who do, spoken just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoodoo is folk magic or a spell bringing bad luck.

clue.text: Two seamen, one from central Asia

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tar is a sailor
second meaning: a member of the Turkic Tatar people

explanation.walkthrough: The seamen read as a pair of sailors, each a tar, one of whom seems to hail from Asia.

indicators.note: a return is a going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a grid is a network, such as the electricity grid

explanation.surface: Grief at the comeback of a drug-dealing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song for the dead, an elegy.

clue.text: Maybe Aristotle is to follow, riding donkey

an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: a revelling crowd is wild and disorderly, so these letters are thrown about

clue.text: Make too much of old judge holding vicar back

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.walkthrough: Rev. is the written abbreviation of Reverend, the title of a vicar.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an agent who arranges deals between parties
second meaning: more broke, the comparative of broke

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a struggling agent; the second half is the comparative of broke, short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an intermediary who negotiates sales for others; brokest-style comparatives give a poorer person.
